Sensor Lock offers system-wide camera and microphone privacy. The main button has independent sensor switches; Quick Settings has a separate selector. You can block or allow the selected sensors and verify the real state of both sensors.
Android apps may request camera or microphone access at different times. Sensor Lock gives you a deliberate privacy switch so you can keep both sensors blocked when you do not want them available.

For first setup or repair, Android requires Wireless debugging and therefore a Wi-Fi connection. Internet access is not required. After setup, normal use does not need Wi-Fi or internet while the local service remains active.
No account, ads, analytics, tracking or cloud backend. Sensor Lock does not upload camera/microphone state or personal data. Website, GitHub and Google Play links open only when you choose them.

The local privileged service can be stopped by a reboot or by Android. Sensor Lock automatically tries to restore it when Wi-Fi is available. Recovery can take several seconds after a restart. Manual re-pairing is only needed if the saved Android pairing is no longer usable.

Full source code, documentation and the public release APK are available at github.com/eluqen/sensor-lock. Sensor Lock application code is released under Apache License 2.0; bundled third-party components keep their own licenses.

After entering the code, Sensor Lock finds the local pairing port and connects automatically. Wait for completion; the notification disappears after a verified connection.

The first setup uses Android Wireless debugging to bootstrap a local shell-privileged service on the same device. Normal protection commands then use a local on-device connection instead of an internet service.

Camera and microphone are always verified separately. Mixed means their actual Android privacy states differ, even if your currently selected sensor is protected. Sensor selection changes only the next action, never Android privacy settings on its own.
Designed for Android phones and tablets running Android 11 (API 30) or later. No root access is required. Manufacturer-specific Android changes may affect Wireless debugging or automatic recovery.

WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS is granted locally during setup so Sensor Lock can manage temporary setup settings. INTERNET is used for the local ADB socket during pairing or repair; the app has no cloud API endpoint. Notification permission is used for pairing input and reconnect alerts. Boot access is used to attempt recovery after a restart.

After a phone or tablet restart, Sensor Lock automatically restores its local service when Wi-Fi is available. Android Wireless debugging may be enabled briefly during recovery and Android may show its own system notification. Internet access is not required. Recovery can take tens of seconds; a reconnect prompt is shown only if automatic recovery does not succeed.
Sensor Lock is developed and published by ELUQEN, an engineering and technology brand focused on electronics, embedded systems, hardware and software.
